Test "Messaging Test: Premium vs Convenience Framing" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with random assignment to one of two message frames: Premium (emphasizing Swiss engineering, professional quality, and convenience) vs Convenience (emphasizing integrated grinder, time-saving, and hassle-free preparation). Participants are shown a description of a Franke coffee machine and asked to indicate willingness to pay (WTP) and purchase intent on a 7-point scale.. Sample: 500 adult consumers in Germany and Switzerland, screened for interest in coffee and willingness to pay at least €200 for a home machine.. Measure: Average WTP (in euros) and purchase intent (1‑10 scale) for the assigned message frame.. Predictions: T1: Higher average WTP and purchase intent for the Premium frame compared to the Convenience frame.; T2: Higher average WTP and purchase intent for the Convenience frame compared to the Premium frame.. Decision rule: If the average WTP for the Premium frame exceeds the average WTP for the Convenience frame by at least €30, proceed to develop a differentiated premium consumer proposition. sources.excerpt: AquaChek pool and spa test strips are said by manufacturer Hach Company / ETS to be the world’s number one brand in the sector. Products are sold under the AquaChek, AccuGrow and TruTest brands, and include the AquaChek Salt System Test Kit, AquaChek Silver, and TruTest Digital Test Strip Reader, and AquaChek Pro and Pro II.

Once treated water leaves the plant, it can come in contact with various components within the distribution system that potentially alter the quality of the water before it reaches consumers. This makes it hard to guarantee quality for the customer and emphasizes the importance of testing samples in the field.

Drinking water test kits (home test kits) are widely available at hardware stores and the internet, allowing customers to independently assess their drinking water quality at their tap. These kits provide several tests, including: pesticides, bacteria, lead, copper, nitrate, nitrite, iron, chlorine, pH, hardness, and alkalinity.

Home test kit results should be considered an initial step, not a final result. A poor water quality result by a kit should be confirmed with follow-up analyses by a laboratory that uses state-of-the-art instruments, certified methods, and quality control measures to ensure accuracy and reliability.

Hach’s products serve customers ranging from municipal drinking and wastewater to food, power, chemical production, and every other industry that uses water in its processes. As a wholly owned subsidiary of the global corporation Veralto, Hach is equipped with the resources to provide innovative analytical solutions.

In 2010, bystanders administered CPR in 61 percent of public cases and 28.3 percent of in-home cases. In 2014, the rate of bystander CPR rose to 70.6 percent of public cases and 41.3 percent of in-home cases.

Laerdal Medical is a global leader in healthcare education and resuscitation training, using advanced technology and data-driven insights to improve survival rates and enhance the quality of care. We empower our heroes and lifesavers – healthcare professionals – to help them save more lives.

CPR Anytime is a flexible program that allows you to learn CPR at your own pace, in the comfort and privacy of your home. The kits can also facilitate large CPR training programs in school, workplace, or community settings. The kit is portable, making it easy to share with family members or close friends – resulting in more people trained.

At a time marked by geopolitical instability, war in Europe, and growing demands for national preparedness, Laerdal is strengthening its focus on competence, learning, and collaboration in emergency medical services, both civilian and military.

LEBANON – The intensive care nursery (ICN) at Children’s Hospital at Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center (CHaD), New Hampshire’s only children’s hospital, recently received a donation of 500 Infant CPR Anytime kits from the American Heart Association (AHA), funded by the Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield Foundation. The kits contain tools to help new parents learn the lifesaving skills of infant CPR and infant choking relief in as little as 20 minutes and are being distributed to families being discharged from the ICN.

Sample: 300 adult consumers recruited via an online panel, balanced across the two groups (150 per group). Recruitment targets homeowners and small business owners with limited space.. Measure: Purchase intent (binary) and maximum willingness to pay (EUR). Secondary measure: stated primary purchase driver (convenience vs sustainability).. Predictions: T1: Group A will show higher purchase intent and higher average willingness to pay than Group B.; T2: Group B will show higher purchase intent and higher average willingness to pay than Group A.. Test "Consumer Messaging Test: Safety Necessity vs Lifestyle Positioning" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Participants are recruited from a panel of homeowners and style-conscious consumers. Each participant sees one of two product descriptions for the same Dräger consumer device (e.g., a CO alarm or breathalyzer). The safety‑necessity version emphasizes home safety risks and regulatory compliance. The lifestyle version emphasizes design, brand prestige, and fashion appeal. After viewing the description, participants indicate purchase intent on a 7‑point scale (1‑10) and maximum price they would pay.. Sample: 300 participants (150 homeowners, 150 style-conscious consumers) recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and geographic region.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) and maximum price willingness to pay for each messaging condition.. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay for the safety‑necessity version compared to the lifestyle version.; T2: Higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay for the lifestyle version compared to the safety‑necessity version.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent for the safety‑necessity version is at least 1.5 points higher than the lifestyle version, proceed to develop a consumer proposition focused on safety necessity. If the lifestyle version exceeds the safety‑necessity version by at least 1.5 points, develop a lifestyle/fashion proposition. If the difference is below 1.5 points, no expansion is recommended.. Cost: 18000 euros, 8 weeks.

Test "Premium vs Convenience Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Participants view one of two product descriptions for a Franke coffee machine (premium positioning vs convenience positioning) and are asked to indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and maximum price they would pay. A control group sees no description.. Sample: 300 adult consumers interested in coffee, recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and geographic region.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) and maximum price willingness to pay.. Predictions: T1: Premium group will show higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay than convenience group.; T2: Convenience group will show higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay than premium group.. Decision rule: If premium group average purchase intent ≥ 7.5 and its average willingness to pay ≥ €150, proceed to develop a premium consumer proposition. If convenience group average purchase intent ≥ 7.5 and its average willingness to pay ≥ €150, develop a convenience‑focused proposition. If neither group meets its threshold, do not expand.. Cost: 15000 euros, 8 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated premium consumer proposition targeting quality-conscious home consumers, leveraging Swiss engineering and premium positioning. Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated premium consumer proposition targeting quality-conscious home consumers, leveraging Swiss engineering and premium positioning. Who benefits: Individual consumers seeking specialized protection for activities where standard gloves fail.. Why behaviour changes: Shifting from generic industrial gloves to purpose-built, stylish gloves creates a perceived value that justifies higher price and multiple purchases.. How value is captured: Ansell can capture value through premium pricing, brand differentiation, and potential licensing of the specialized design to third-party consumer brands.. Assumptions: Consumers are willing to pay a premium for specialized protective gear.; The differentiated product can be produced at scale without compromising quality.; The brand can be effectively positioned as premium and specialized in the consumer market.. Predictions: Surveyed consumers will indicate willingness to pay at least 20% more for a specialized glove compared to standard gloves.; Purchase intent for the specialized glove will be higher among consumers who engage in outdoor activities than among those who do not.; Repeat purchase rate for the specialized glove will be higher than for standard gloves..

T2: Consumers will adopt differentiated protective gloves for specific use cases if they perceive the product as a health and safety requirement, leading to purchase driven by compliance and regulatory standards rather than style or premium positioning. Who benefits: Healthcare professionals, industrial workers, and regulatory entities requiring compliant protective gear.. Why behaviour changes: Compliance and regulatory mandates increase the perceived necessity of protective gloves, prompting purchases even if the product is not perceived as stylish or premium.. How value is captured: Ansell can capture value through higher volume sales to industrial and healthcare segments, potential licensing of compliant designs, and partnerships with regulatory bodies.. Assumptions: Regulatory compliance is a primary driver for purchase decisions in the target segments.; The differentiated product meets or exceeds the required standards without compromising functionality.; The brand can be effectively positioned as compliant and reliable in the consumer market.. Predictions: Purchase intent for the differentiated glove will be higher among buyers who must comply with specific safety standards than among buyers who purchase for non-compliance reasons.; Sales of the differentiated glove will be concentrated in regions with strict safety regulations.; Repeat purchase rate will be lower than for standard gloves due to the compliance-driven nature of the purchase..

Test "Consumer Messaging Test for Specialized Glove" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized exposure to two different product descriptions of a differentiated glove for a specific use case (e.g., outdoor recreation). Participants are randomly assigned to one of the two descriptions and asked to indicate willingness to pay (WTP) and purchase intent on a 7-point scale. A control group receives a neutral description.. Sample: 300 adult consumers recruited via an online panel, balanced between outdoor recreation and non-recreation segments.. Measure: Average willingness to pay (WTP) in euros for the specialized glove, and purchase intent on a 7-point scale.. Predictions: T1: Participants exposed to the specialized, premium description will have a WTP at least 20% higher and purchase intent at least 15% higher than those exposed to the neutral description.; T2: Participants exposed to the specialized, premium description will have a WTP at least 20% higher and purchase intent at least 15% higher than those exposed to the neutral description.. Decision rule: If the average WTP for the specialized description exceeds the neutral description by at least 20% AND the purchase intent for the specialized description exceeds the neutral description by at least 15%, proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition. If the difference is less than 20% for either WTP or purchase intent, do not invest in a differentiated proposition.. Cost: 20000 euros, 8 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., outdoor recreation) that emphasizes premium design, superior protection, and style. Begin with a small-scale pilot test to validate consumer willingness to pay and purchase intent before scaling. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., outdoor recreation) that emphasizes premium design, superior protection, and style. Target customer: Outdoor recreation enthusiasts and consumers who engage in activities where standard gloves fail, such as hiking, cycling, and gardening.. Value proposition: A purpose-built, stylish protective glove that offers enhanced protection and durability, positioned as a premium item that combines functionality with aesthetic appeal.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Consumer Messaging Test (or a similar experiment) to measure willingness to pay and purchase intent for a specialized glove description.. Uncertainty: The exact size of the consumer market for differentiated protective gloves and the willingness to pay a premium are uncertain. Additionally, the competitive landscape and Ansell's ability to differentiate in a crowded market are unknown.. Would change if: If the pilot test shows a willingness to pay difference of less than 20% or purchase intent difference of less than 15% between the specialized and neutral descriptions, the investment would be reconsidered in favor of no expansion.; If new evidence shows that regulatory compliance is the primary driver of consumer purchases, the recommendation would shift toward a compliance-focused proposition.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Why behaviour changes: Current consumer scales lack precision; a scale that measures by weight reliably reduces guesswork and improves recipe accuracy.. How value is captured: Mettler-Toledo can charge a premium for precision features and sell through direct channels, leveraging its brand reputation for accuracy.. Predictions: In a test offering a precision digital scale to home cooks, purchase intent will be higher than for a standard digital scale.; Willingness to pay will be above the price of a standard scale by at least 20%..

Test "Precision vs Health Messaging Digital Scale Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging test. Participants are recruited from a panel of home cooks and health-conscious consumers. Each participant sees one of two product descriptions: a precision-focused description emphasizing accurate weight measurement for recipes, and a health-focused description emphasizing portion control and carbohydrate counting. After viewing the description, they are asked to indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale), maximum price they would pay, and likelihood to purchase. The test is run in two rounds: round 1 presents the precision description; round 2 presents the health description. The decision rule is: if purchase intent for the health description is at least 10 points higher than for the precision description, proceed with a health‑focused proposition; otherwise, proceed with a precision‑focused proposition. The test budget is €20,000 and the 12‑week. Sample: 300 participants (150 per condition), recruited from an online panel of home cooks and health-conscious consumers in the United States.. Measure: Purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and maximum price willingness to pay.. Predictions: T1: Purchase intent for the precision description will be at least 10 points higher than for the health description, and willingness to pay will be above the price of a precision scale by at least 20%.; T2: Purchase intent for the health description will be at least 10 points higher than for the precision description, and willingness to pay will be above the price of a health‑focused scale by at least 15%.. Decision rule: If the health description's purchase intent is at least 10 points higher than the precision description, proceed with a health‑focused consumer proposition. If the precision description's purchase intent is at least 10 points higher, proceed with a precision‑focused proposition. If neither condition is met, do not expand into a differentiated consumer. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes precision weight measurement for home cooks, targeting a specific use case such as recipe accuracy and portion control. Total revenue for 2025 is expected to be USD 33.3 million dollar with 7% growth in the Business segment and 21% growth in the Pro segment, while Consumer revenues decreased 20% following the strategic decision to prioritize margin improvement.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether there is sufficient public evidence to justify Belimo Holding AG investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current HVAC actuators, valves, and sensors, sold to commercial building manufacturers and through controls contractors and system integrators.. Constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Evidence must demonstrate consumer demand, willingness to pay, or a viable route to market for a differentiated consumer proposition.; Any recommendation must consider Belimo’s existing B2B business model and current reach to individual buyers.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., residential home automation, DIY HVAC control, or a new consumer segment).; 2) Expand the existing B2B product portfolio with new features or packaging without targeting consumers directly.; 3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on commercial building manufacturers and system integrators.; 4) Change the route to market (e.g., direct-to-consumer e‑commerce, partnerships with home‑im improvement retailers, or a subscription model for home control services).; 5) Target a different customer group within the commercial segment (e.g., small‑to‑medium office buildings, residential building owners, or energy‑efficient retrofits)..

Test "Safety vs Energy Efficiency Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated product offers. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two message conditions: Safety Condition (emphasizes safety-critical, reliable residential HVAC control) or Energy Condition (emphasizes energy‑efficiency and cost savings). Both conditions present a Belimo residential control system at a fixed price point. Participants indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and maximum price they would pay.. Sample: 500 U.S. homeowners (250 per condition) recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, income, and home ownership status.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) and maximum price willingness to pay for each condition.. Predictions: T1: Safety Condition will generate higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay than Energy Condition.; T2: Energy Condition will generate higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay than Safety Condition.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent in the Safety Condition is at least 10 points higher than in the Energy Condition (i.e., Safety ≥ Energy + 10), we conclude T1 is supported. If the difference is less than 10 points, we conclude neither theory is strongly supported. If the difference is less than €10, we conclude no significant difference and recommend further market research.. Cost: 2000 euros, 4 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes safety-critical, reliable residential HVAC control, leveraging Belimo’s commercial reputation for durability and technical excellence. Begin with a limited pilot offering through retail partners to test homeowner willingness to pay a premium for safety messaging. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

T1 kept: Simulated evidence SYN-D concerns a warehouse label printer and packing errors, which does not address homeowner motivations for safety-critical features or willingness to pay a premium for them. Therefore it does not affect T1. New claim: Homeowners will adopt a differentiated Belimo consumer proposition if they perceive it as a safety-critical, reliable solution for their home HVAC system, because they trust Belimo's reputation for durability and technical excellence in commercial applications.. Evidence: SYN-D.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes safety-critical, reliable residential HVAC control, leveraging Belimo’s commercial reputation for durability and technical excellence. Begin with a limited pilot offering through retail partners to test homeowner willingness to pay a premium for safety messaging. Target customer: Homeowners who prioritize safety and reliability in their HVAC control system, particularly those who are risk‑averse and prefer brands with a proven track record in commercial applications.. Value proposition: A Belimo residential control system marketed as a safety‑critical, reliable solution that builds on the brand’s existing reputation for durability and technical excellence, offering peace of mind and reduced perceived risk of failure.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Safety vs Energy Efficiency Messaging Test (500 U.S. homeowners, two message conditions, purchase intent and price willingness) to quantify the premium homeowners are willing to pay for safety messaging.. Uncertainty: The size of the consumer market for Belimo and the actual willingness to pay a premium for safety‑critical features remain uncertain. The test will provide data to resolve this uncertainty.. Would change if: If the test shows the Energy Condition generates significantly higher purchase intent and willingness to pay than the Safety Condition, we would shift focus to energy‑efficiency messaging and consider a different consumer proposition.; If the test shows no significant difference between the two conditions, we would recommend further market research to better understand homeowner motivations and the size of the consumer market.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

sources.excerpt: The Dishwasher has three standard wash cycles that clean approximately 40/28/24 racks per hour, making this ideal for the busy kitchen.

The food service industry, hotels, bakeries, butchers and industrial caterers trust in the high-end commercial warewashing solutions from Winterhalter. All Winterhalter machines are manufactured in Germany or Switzerland and stand apart because of their high quality, low operating costs and sustainable use of resources.

Customers have their UC customised precisely to their specific needs as a glasswasher, dishwasher, cutlery washer or bistro warewasher in one of four sizes: S, M, L or XL.

In 2010, bystanders administered CPR in 61 percent of public cases and 28.3 percent of in-home cases. In 2014, the rate of bystander CPR rose to 70.6 percent of public cases and 41.3 percent of in-home cases.

Laerdal Medical is a global leader in healthcare education and resuscitation training, using advanced technology and data-driven insights to improve survival rates and enhance the quality of care. We empower our heroes and lifesavers – healthcare professionals – to help them save more lives.

CPR Anytime is a flexible program that allows you to learn CPR at your own pace, in the comfort and privacy of your home. The kits can also facilitate large CPR training programs in school, workplace, or community settings. The kit is portable, making it easy to share with family members or close friends – resulting in more people trained.

At a time marked by geopolitical instability, war in Europe, and growing demands for national preparedness, Laerdal is strengthening its focus on competence, learning, and collaboration in emergency medical services, both civilian and military.

LEBANON – The intensive care nursery (ICN) at Children’s Hospital at Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center (CHaD), New Hampshire’s only children’s hospital, recently received a donation of 500 Infant CPR Anytime kits from the American Heart Association (AHA), funded by the Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield Foundation. The kits contain tools to help new parents learn the lifesaving skills of infant CPR and infant choking relief in as little as 20 minutes and are being distributed to families being discharged from the ICN.

Test "Consumer Messaging Test: Safety vs Health Routine" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Participants are recruited from a panel of health-conscious consumers (n=500). Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: Group A receives a safety/peace-of-mind message about home CPR training (e.g., "Be prepared to save a life with home CPR training."). Group B receives a health/routine message (e.g., "Add home CPR training to your daily wellness routine."). Both groups see a product description of a portable home CPR kit and are asked to indicate willingness to pay (WTP) and likelihood to purchase on a 7-point scale (1‑2 "Very unlikely" to 7 "Very likely").. Sample: 500 health-conscious consumers recruited from an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and geographic region.. Measure: Average willingness to pay (WTP) and purchase intent (likelihood to purchase) for each messaging group.. Predictions: T1: Group A will show higher average WTP and purchase intent than Group B because the safety message directly addresses life-saving motivation.; T2: Group B will show higher average WTP and purchase intent than Group A because the health/routine message aligns with existing health habits.. Decision rule: If the average WTP for Group A is at least 1.5 times the average WTP for Group B (i.e., WTP_A ≥ 1.5 × WTP_B), proceed to develop a safety‑focused consumer proposition. sources.excerpt: DANBURY, Conn. — Belimo Americas, a manufacturer of damper actuators and control valves for commercial HVAC, announced the availability of products for residential applications with select actuators, round damper assemblies, and pressure bypass damper controls.

Total revenue for 2025 is expected to be USD 33.3 million dollar with 7% growth in the Business segment and 21% growth in the Pro segment, while Consumer revenues decreased 20% following the strategic decision to prioritize margin improvement.

Gross profit grew year-on-year in the Business and Pro segments, while gross profit in the Consumer segment was impacted negatively by a weakening US consumer sentiment, US tariffs and costs related to promotions and campaigns with key retail partners.

Belimo is a global market leader in the development, production, and sales of field devices for the energy-efficient control of heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems. The focus of its core business is on damper actuators, control valves, sensors and meters.

With an emphasis on product quality, durability with minimal maintenance, and highly innovative, technically advanced solutions, the Company has become a preferred choice in high-performance applications in large commercial buildings such as data centers, hospitals, schools and universities, offices, governmental buildings, infrastructure and industrial sites.

Belimo collaborates closely with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) of HVAC systems and system integrators who incorporate Belimo products into large-scale HVAC projects. It provides them with extensive technical support, including planning, customization, calibration, and troubleshooting – and conducts training for HVAC professionals to optimize installation effectiveness.
In addition to our growing portfolio of DIY solutions sold through top retail and e-commerce channels, the majority of our technologies are installed by professionals.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether there is sufficient public evidence to justify Belimo Holding AG investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current HVAC actuators, valves, and sensors, sold to commercial building manufacturers and through controls contractors and system integrators.. Predictions: In a test offering a Belimo residential kit at a 10% premium, purchase intent will be at least 15% higher than for a generic equivalent.; Surveyed homeowners will rank reliability and brand trust as top purchase drivers..

T1: Consumers will adopt Belimo residential products if they perceive them as reliable, energy‑efficient, and easy to install, because they value performance and lower long‑term costs. Who benefits: Homeowners seeking efficient HVAC control and DIYers who prefer plug‑and‑play solutions.. Why behaviour changes: Growing awareness of energy savings and the availability of zone‑based residential control make consumers willing to choose Belimo over generic or competitor products.. How value is captured: Belimo can capture value by pricing premium on quality, durability, and support, and by selling through retail and e‑commerce channels at higher margins.. Assumptions: Consumers currently purchase HVAC control products primarily through professionals or large‑scale OEMs.; Belimo can communicate its technical advantages to individual buyers.; Retail/online channels will stock and promote Belimo residential products effectively.. T2: Consumers will adopt Belimo residential products if they perceive them as a status or brand signal, because they value prestige and the association with a trusted, high‑performance HVAC brand. Who benefits: Affluent homeowners and early adopters who seek to signal sophistication and reliability in their home automation choices.. Why behaviour changes: Consumers increasingly view products as a reflection of personal taste and lifestyle, and Belimo’s reputation for technical excellence and durability makes it an attractive premium choice.. How value is captured: Belimo can capture value by positioning its residential products as a premium, brand‑driven offering, allowing higher price points and limited edition designs, and by leveraging its existing OEM relationships to reach niche markets.. Assumptions: Consumers are willing to pay a premium for brand prestige in home automation.; Belimo’s brand perception can be effectively communicated to individual buyers.; A limited‑edition or exclusive product line can generate demand without overwhelming production capacity.. Test "Residential Product Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized product exposure and willingness-to-pay (WTP) questions.. Sample: 500 U.S. homeowners (ages 25-55) who have considered purchasing a new HVAC control product in the past 12 months, recruited via an online panel.. Measure: 1) Purchase intent: binary (will buy) or intent to purchase within 12 weeks. 2) WTP: maximum price a respondent would pay for a Belimo residential zone damper. 3) Messaging preference: ranking Belimo vs. competitor on energy efficiency, durability, and brand prestige.. Predictions: T1: At least 20% of respondents will express purchase intent and indicate a WTP at least 10% above the competitor's average WTP, with higher energy-efficiency and durability rankings.; T2: At least 15% of respondents will express purchase intent and indicate a WTP at least 10% above the competitor's average WTP, with higher brand prestige and status rankings.. Decision rule: If purchase intent >=20% AND (Belimo WTP >= competitor WTP + 10% OR Belimo prestige ranking >= competitor prestige ranking), proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition. If purchase intent <20% OR Belimo WTP < competitor WTP - 10%, do not invest in a consumer proposition. If both conditions fail, maintain B2B focus.. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

Favours T1: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition at this time. Public evidence shows Belimo already offers residential zone solutions and is a market leader in HVAC control, but there is no demonstrated consumer demand, willingness to pay, or clear route to market. The recommended next action is to conduct a targeted test (e.g., a willingness-to-pay survey) before committing resources. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition at this time. Public evidence shows Belimo already offers residential zone solutions and is a market leader in HVAC control, but there is no demonstrated consumer demand, willingness to pay, or clear route to market. The recommended next action is to conduct a targeted test (e.g., a willingness-to-pay survey) before committing resources. Target customer: Homeowners and DIYers who have considered purchasing a new HVAC control product in the past 12 months, particularly those seeking energy-efficient and easy-to-install residential control solutions.. Value proposition: A premium, energy-efficient residential HVAC control product that leverages Belimo’s technical leadership and durability, sold through retail and e‑commerce channels with support for installation and calibration.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed 10‑week willingness-to-pay survey test (500 U.S. homeowners) to measure purchase intent and price sensitivity against competitors.. Uncertainty: The size of the consumer market, actual willingness to pay, and the ability to reach individual buyers through existing OEM and integrator channels remain uncertain.. Would change if: If the test shows purchase intent below 20% or Belimo’s price is significantly below competitors by at least 10%, the investment case would weaken and the recommendation would shift toward maintaining B2B focus.; If new evidence shows strong consumer demand for a status/brand proposition (e.g., premium pricing and limited editions), the recommendation would shift toward developing a differentiated consumer proposition targeting affluent homeowners.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

KGaA should invest in creating a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current B2B portable and stationary measuring instruments, based on evidence of market demand, competitive positioning, and feasibility within budget and time constraints.. Constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Current consumer reach is unknown; must be discovered from public sources.; Any new proposition must be justified by evidence of consumer demand, willingness to pay, and competitive advantage.; Investment decision must consider risk, resource allocation, and potential impact on existing B2B operations.. Test "Consumer Messaging Test: Energy Efficiency vs. Diagnostic Focus" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Participants are recruited from a panel of homeowners and small business owners. Participants view a product description of a Testo measuring instrument and are asked to indicate purchase intent (1-7 scale) and willingness to pay (EUR). The description is presented with one of two messaging frames: (1) energy efficiency and DIY savings (T1) or (2) professional-grade diagnostic capability for home issues (T2). A control group sees no message.. Sample: 300 participants (150 per arm) recruited via an online panel to ensure demographic diversity. Participants must have experienced home energy concerns or maintenance issues in the past year.. Measure: Primary measure: average purchase intent score (1-7) for each messaging arm. Secondary measure: average willingness to pay (EUR) for each arm.. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and willingness to pay in the energy efficiency messaging arm compared to the diagnostic arm.; T2: Higher purchase intent and willingness to pay in the diagnostic messaging arm compared to the energy efficiency arm.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent for the energy efficiency arm is at least 1.5 points higher than the diagnostic arm (e.g., 5.5 vs. 4.0), proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition focused on energy efficiency. Test "Consumer Messaging Test for Specialized vs Compliance Glove" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Participants are recruited from outdoor recreation and general consumer segments. Each participant views one of two product descriptions of a differentiated glove: (1) Premium specialized glove emphasizing superior protection and style; (2) Compliance glove emphasizing regulatory requirement and safety certification. After viewing, participants indicate willingness to pay (WTP) and purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑10).. Sample: 300 participants (150 outdoor recreation enthusiasts and 150 general consumers), balanced across gender and age. Randomly assigned to see either premium or compliance message.. Predictions: T1: Group A will show higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay at the premium price compared to Group B.; T2: Group B will show higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay at the low-cost price compared to Group A.. If Group B's purchase intent rate exceeds Group A's by at least 10 percentage points at the low-cost price, proceed with a low-cost proposition. If neither threshold is met, do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition.. Cost: 18000 euros, 8 weeks.

Test "Digital Messaging Test: SEAI vs Premium Messaging" between T1; T2. Method: Run a targeted online survey with two equal arms: Arm A receives a message emphasizing SEAI grant support and the One Stop Shop process; Arm B receives a message emphasizing premium thermal performance and durability. Both arms include a willingness-to-pay (WTP) question. Recruit 500 homeowners in the UK who have shown interest in home insulation (via a pre‐screen). Randomly assign participants to either Arm A or Arm B, then collect responses to the WTP question.. Sample: 500 homeowners in the UK who have shown interest in home insulation (pre‐screen).. Measure: Willingness-to-pay (WTP) for Kingspan's product, measured in euros.. Predictions: T1: Arm A will show a significantly higher WTP than Arm B, because homeowners trust the grant process and are motivated by public funding.; T2: Arm B will show a significantly higher WTP than Arm A, because homeowners value premium performance and are willing to pay more for superior thermal efficiency.. Decision rule: If the average WTP in Arm A is at least 20% higher than in Arm B, proceed with developing a consumer proposition that emphasizes SEAI grant support (supporting T1). If Arm B's WTP is at least 20% higher than Arm A, proceed with a premium positioning (supporting T2). If the difference is less than 20% or both arms are equal, do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition yet.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Test "Consumer Messaging Test: Personal Responsibility vs. Mandate" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants are recruited from a panel of homeowners (n=300). Each participant sees one of two product descriptions for a home safety device (a gas detector) and is asked to indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and maximum price they would pay. The two descriptions differ only in framing: Condition A frames the device as a personal protective equipment for everyday home use, emphasizing individual responsibility. Condition B frames it as a health insurance or employer mandate requirement, emphasizing compliance. Participants are randomly assigned to see either condition.. Sample: 300 homeowners recruited from an online panel, balanced across gender and age. Randomly assigned to see either Condition A or Condition B.. Measure: Purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and maximum price willingness to pay for each condition.. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay in Condition A (personal responsibility framing) compared to Condition B.; T2: Higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay in Condition B (mandate framing) compared to Condition A.. Decision rule: If the difference in average purchase intent between Condition A and Condition B is at least 1.5 points (e.g., Condition A ≥ 6.5 and Condition B ≤ 5.0), conclude the framing that aligns with the theory is supported. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, both theories remain plausible and further testing is needed.. Cost: 18000 euros, 6 weeks.

sources.excerpt: In 2010, bystanders administered CPR in 61 percent of public cases and 28.3 percent of in-home cases. In 2014, the rate of bystander CPR rose to 70.6 percent of public cases and 41.3 percent of in-home cases.
Today, more than 350,000 cardiac arrests occur outside of hospitals in the United States annually. Nearly three out of four of those cardiac arrests happen in homes.

Laerdal Medical is a global leader in healthcare education and resuscitation training, using advanced technology and data-driven insights to improve survival rates and enhance the quality of care. We empower our heroes and lifesavers – healthcare professionals – to help them save more lives.

CPR Anytime is a flexible program that allows you to learn CPR at your own pace, in the comfort and privacy of your home. The kits can also facilitate large CPR training programs in school, workplace, or community settings. The kit is portable, making it easy to share with family members or close friends – resulting in more people trained.

At a time marked by geopolitical instability, war in Europe, and growing demands for national preparedness, Laerdal is strengthening its focus on competence, learning, and collaboration in emergency medical services, both civilian and military.

LEBANON – The intensive care nursery (ICN) at Children’s Hospital at Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center (CHaD), New Hampshire’s only children’s hospital, recently received a donation of 500 Infant CPR Anytime kits from the American Heart Association (AHA), funded by the Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield Foundation. The kits contain tools to help new parents learn the lifesaving skills of infant CPR and infant choking relief in as little as 20 minutes and are being distributed to families being discharged from the ICN.

Test "Consumer Messaging Test for Home CPR Training" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging conditions. Participants are recruited from a panel of health-conscious adults (n=300). They are randomly assigned to one of three conditions: (1) Personal health responsibility messaging (emphasizing individual preparedness and family safety); (2) Health routine integration messaging (emphasizing convenience and alignment with existing health habits); (3) Authority endorsement messaging (emphasizing endorsement by trusted health authorities). Participants are asked to indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and maximum price they would pay for the product.. Sample: 300 health-conscious adults recruited via an online panel, balanced across the three conditions.. Measure: Purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and maximum price willingness to pay for the home CPR training kit.. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and willingness to pay in the personal health responsibility condition compared to the other two conditions.; T2: Higher purchase intent and willingness to pay in the health routine integration condition compared to the other two conditions.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent in the personal health responsibility condition is at least 10 points higher than in the health routine integration condition, and the difference is statistically significant (p<0.05), then T1 is supported and the recommendation is to develop a differentiated consumer proposition focused on personal health responsibility. If the average purchase intent in the health routine integration condition is at least 10 points higher than in the personal health responsibility condition, and the difference is statistically significant (p<0.05), then T2 is supported and the recommendation is to develop a differentiated consumer proposition focused on health routine integration. sources.excerpt: DANBURY, Conn. — Belimo Americas, a manufacturer of damper actuators and control valves for commercial HVAC, announced the availability of products for residential applications with select actuators, round damper assemblies, and pressure bypass damper controls.

Total revenue for 2025 is expected to be USD 33.3 million dollar with 7% growth in the Business segment and 21% growth in the Pro segment, while Consumer revenues decreased 20% following the strategic decision to prioritize margin improvement.

Gross profit grew year-on-year in the Business and Pro segments, while gross profit in the Consumer segment was impacted negatively by a weakening US consumer sentiment, US tariffs and costs related to promotions and campaigns with key retail partners.

Belimo is a global market leader in the development, production, and sales of field devices for the energy-efficient control of heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems. The focus of its core business is on damper actuators, control valves, sensors and meters.

With an emphasis on product quality, durability with minimal maintenance, and highly innovative, technically advanced solutions, the Company has become a preferred choice in high-performance applications in large commercial buildings such as data centers, hospitals, schools and universities, offices, governmental buildings, infrastructure and industrial sites.

Belimo collaborates closely with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) of HVAC systems and system integrators who incorporate Belimo products into large-scale HVAC projects. It provides them with extensive technical support, including planning, customization, calibration, and troubleshooting – and conducts training for HVAC professionals to optimize installation effectiveness.
The company’s first product launch of 2020 offers HVAC contractors reliable, high-quality solutions with precise performance and offers the value-conscious homeowner a wider range of options.
In addition to our growing portfolio of DIY solutions sold through top retail and e-commerce channels, the majority of our technologies are installed by professionals.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether there is sufficient public evidence to justify Belimo Holding AG investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current HVAC actuators, valves, and sensors, sold to commercial building manufacturers and through controls contractors and system integrators.. Constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Evidence must demonstrate consumer demand, willingness to pay, or a viable route to market for a differentiated consumer proposition.; Any recommendation must consider Belimo’s existing B2B business model and current reach to individual buyers.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., residential home automation, DIY HVAC control, or a new consumer segment).; 2) Expand the existing B2B product portfolio with new features or packaging without targeting consumers directly.; 3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on commercial building manufacturers and system integrators.; 4) Change the route to market (e.g., direct-to-consumer e‑commerce, partnerships with home‑im improvement retailers, or a subscription model for home control services).; 5) Target a different customer group within the commercial segment (e.g., small‑to‑medium office buildings, residential building owners, or energy‑efficient retrofits)..

Test "Home Ice Machine Purchase Intent Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated purchase scenarios and willingness-to-pay (WTP) questions.. Sample: 500 U.S. residential consumers (aged 18-55) recruited via an online panel, balanced for gender and geographic region.. Measure: Purchase intent (binary: would buy) and maximum WTP (EUR) for a differentiated home ice machine featuring either convenience or health/unpasteurized ice features.. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and WTP for the convenience-focused unit than for the health-focused unit.; T2: Higher purchase intent and WTP for the health-focused unit than for the convenience-focused unit.. Decision rule: If the average WTP for the convenience-focused unit exceeds the health-focused unit's WTP by at least 15% (e.g., €120 vs €105), proceed to develop a convenience-focused consumer proposition. If the opposite difference holds, develop a health-focused proposition. If the difference is within 10%, conduct a. Cost: 18000 euros, 8 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes convenience and the desire for fresh, chewable ice at home, rather than health/unpasteurized ice. Use the proposed purchase intent test to validate demand before committing resources. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes convenience and the desire for fresh, chewable ice at home, rather than health/unpasteurized ice. Use the proposed purchase intent test to validate demand before committing resources. Target customer: Residential consumers (aged 18-55) seeking convenient, high-quality ice for beverages and food preparation.. Value proposition: A differentiated home ice machine offering convenience, fresh nugget ice, and premium features, sold through retail channels at a premium price.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the 8‑week, €18,000 purchase intent test with 500 U.S. residential consumers to measure willingness to pay for convenience versus health features.. Uncertainty: The size of the consumer market and the willingness to pay for convenience features are unknown. Health‑focused demand may not translate into sales.. Would change if: If the test shows the health‑focused unit achieving a higher average WTP than the convenience‑focused unit by at least 15%, we would shift focus to a health‑focused proposition.; If the test shows no significant difference or a lower difference, we would reconsider the investment or explore other alternatives.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

sources.excerpt: DANBURY, Conn. — Belimo Americas, a manufacturer of damper actuators and control valves for commercial HVAC, announced the availability of products for residential applications with select actuators, round damper assemblies, and pressure bypass damper controls.

Total revenue for 2025 is expected to be USD 33.3 million dollar with 7% growth in the Business segment and 21% growth in the Pro segment, while Consumer revenues decreased 20% following the strategic decision to prioritize margin improvement.

Gross profit grew year-on-year in the Business and Pro segments, while gross profit in the Consumer segment was impacted negatively by a weakening US consumer sentiment, US tariffs and costs related to promotions and campaigns with key retail partners.

Belimo is a global market leader in the development, production, and sales of field devices for the energy-efficient control of heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems. The focus of its core business is on damper actuators, control valves, sensors and meters.

With an emphasis on product quality, durability with minimal maintenance, and highly innovative, technically advanced solutions, the Company has become a preferred choice in high-performance applications in large commercial buildings such as data centers, hospitals, schools and universities, offices, governmental buildings, infrastructure and industrial sites.

Belimo collaborates closely with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) of HVAC systems and system integrators who incorporate Belimo products into large-scale HVAC projects. It provides them with extensive technical support, including planning, customization, calibration, and troubleshooting – and conducts training for HVAC professionals to optimize installation effectiveness.
“Heating systems in Europe are unique and have a variety of hardware and software requirements that make it challenging to build for the diverse set of homes,” Google’s post states.
In addition to our growing portfolio of DIY solutions sold through top retail and e-commerce channels, the majority of our technologies are installed by professionals.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether there is sufficient public evidence to justify Belimo Holding AG investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current HVAC actuators, valves, and sensors, sold to commercial building manufacturers and through controls contractors and system integrators.. Constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Evidence must demonstrate consumer demand, willingness to pay, or a viable route to market for a differentiated consumer proposition.; Any recommendation must consider Belimo’s existing B2B business model and current reach to individual buyers.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., residential home automation, DIY HVAC control, or a new consumer segment).; 2) Expand the existing B2B product portfolio with new features or packaging without targeting consumers directly.; 3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on commercial building manufacturers and system integrators.; 4) Change the route to market (e.g., direct-to-consumer e‑commerce, partnerships with home‑im improvement retailers, or a subscription model for home control services).; 5) Target a different customer group within the commercial segment (e.g., small‑to‑medium office buildings, residential building owners, or energy‑efficient retrofits)..

Test "Premium vs Convenience Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants view a product description of a Franke coffee machine (identical spec) and are offered two price points: a premium price 20% above a comparable entry-level machine and a standard price. They are then asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale (1‑10) and to rank quality and convenience importance.. Sample: 300 adult consumers recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and geographic region to ensure representativeness.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) and importance ranking (quality vs convenience) for each price point.. Predictions: T1: Premium price will generate purchase intent at least 15% higher than standard price, and quality will be ranked higher than convenience.; T2: Convenience message will generate purchase intent at least 15% higher than premium price, and convenience will be ranked higher than quality.. Decision rule: If premium price purchase intent ≥ 15% points higher than standard price AND quality ranking ≥ convenience ranking, proceed to develop a premium consumer proposition. If convenience message purchase intent ≥ 15% points higher than premium price AND convenience ranking ≥ quality ranking, develop a convenience‑focused proposition. If neither condition is met, do not expand.. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated premium consumer proposition targeting home office and small retail segments, leveraging Franke’s professional reputation and convenience features. Conduct a low‑cost messaging test to validate consumer willingness to pay a premium for quality. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

T1 kept: Simulated evidence SYN-D concerns a warehouse label printer and does not address consumer motivation for premium quality or convenience. Therefore it does not affect T1. New claim: none. Evidence: SYN-D.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated premium consumer proposition targeting home office and small retail segments, leveraging Franke’s professional reputation and convenience features. Conduct a low‑cost messaging test to validate consumer willingness to pay a premium for quality. Target customer: Home office professionals and small retail environments (e.g., cafes, hotels) that value professional quality and convenience.. Value proposition: A premium‑priced Franke machine that combines professional‑grade quality, modern design, and convenience features (e.g., integrated grinder, pre‑ground beans, time‑saving automation) to meet the needs of busy consumers.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Premium vs Convenience Messaging Test (300 participants, two price points, purchase intent and importance ranking) to determine whether consumers will pay a premium for quality or convenience.. Uncertainty: The actual willingness to pay a premium price for Franke machines is unknown; the test will provide data on purchase intent and importance rankings. Additionally, the competitive landscape and consumer price sensitivity remain uncertain.. Would change if: If the test shows purchase intent for the premium price is at least 15% lower than for the standard price, indicating insufficient demand for a premium proposition.; If the test shows purchase intent for the convenience message is at least 15% higher than for the premium price, indicating convenience is the primary driver.; If new evidence shows strong consumer demand for Franke machines in specific segments, such as home office or small retail, the recommendation could shift toward expanding into those segments.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

sources.excerpt: DANBURY, Conn. — Belimo Americas, a manufacturer of damper actuators and control valves for commercial HVAC, announced the availability of products for residential applications with select actuators, round damper assemblies, and pressure bypass damper controls.

Total revenue for 2025 is expected to be USD 33.3 million dollar with 7% growth in the Business segment and 21% growth in the Pro segment, while Consumer revenues decreased 20% following the strategic decision to prioritize margin improvement.

Gross profit grew year-on-year in the Business and Pro segments, while gross profit in the Consumer segment was impacted negatively by a weakening US consumer sentiment, US tariffs and costs related to promotions and campaigns with key retail partners.

Belimo is a global market leader in the development, production, and sales of field devices for the energy-efficient control of heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems. The focus of its core business is on damper actuators, control valves, sensors and meters.

With an emphasis on product quality, durability with minimal maintenance, and highly innovative, technically advanced solutions, the Company has become a preferred choice in high-performance applications in large commercial buildings such as data centers, hospitals, schools and universities, offices, governmental buildings, infrastructure and industrial sites.

Belimo collaborates closely with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) of HVAC systems and system integrators who incorporate Belimo products into large-scale HVAC projects. It provides them with extensive technical support, including planning, customization, calibration, and troubleshooting – and conducts training for HVAC professionals to optimize installation effectiveness.
In addition to our growing portfolio of DIY solutions sold through top retail and e-commerce channels, the majority of our technologies are installed by professionals.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether there is sufficient public evidence to justify Belimo Holding AG investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current HVAC actuators, valves, and sensors, sold to commercial building manufacturers and through controls contractors and system integrators.. Constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Evidence must demonstrate consumer demand, willingness to pay, or a viable route to market for a differentiated consumer proposition.; Any recommendation must consider Belimo’s existing B2B business model and current reach to individual buyers.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., residential home automation, DIY HVAC control, or a new consumer segment).; 2) Expand the existing B2B product portfolio with new features or packaging without targeting consumers directly.; 3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on commercial building manufacturers and system integrators.; 4) Change the route to market (e.g., direct-to-consumer e‑commerce, partnerships with home‑im improvement retailers, or a subscription model for home control services).; 5) Target a different customer group within the commercial segment (e.g., small‑to‑medium office buildings, residential building owners, or energy‑efficient retrofits)..

Constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Current consumer reach is unknown; must be discovered from public sources.; Any new proposition must be justified by evidence of consumer demand, willingness to pay, and competitive advantage.; Investment decision must consider risk, resource allocation, and potential impact on existing B2B operations.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., home DIY, small business, or consumer health monitoring) with a new product or service model.; 2) Expand the existing B2B product line into adjacent consumer segments without a differentiated proposition (e.g., add consumer‑focused accessories or services).; 3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on the current B2B market and existing product portfolio.; 4) Change the route to market for existing B2B products to reach consumers directly (e.g., e‑commerce, subscription services) without altering the core product.; 5) Target a different customer group within the B2B segment (e.g., small trades, individual contractors) with a differentiated proposition..

T1: Homeowners will adopt Testo measuring instruments if they perceive the devices as reliable and convenient for DIY energy efficiency tasks, because they value ease of use and trust the brand. Who benefits: Homeowners conducting DIY energy audits or retrofits. Why behaviour changes: They will purchase Testo instruments if they see them recommended by trusted sources and if the instruments simplify their tasks, reducing perceived effort and risk.. How value is captured: Testo can capture value through premium pricing for consumer-friendly versions, direct-to-consumer sales, and potential subscription services for data analysis.. Assumptions: Homeowners are willing to pay a premium for perceived reliability.; Testo can differentiate its consumer offerings from generic DIY tools.; Distribution channels (e.g., online, retail) can reach target homeowners effectively.. Predictions: In a test offering a simplified version of a Testo instrument, purchase intent will be higher than for a standard B2B version.; Surveyed homeowners will cite ease of use as the primary reason for choosing the product..

T2: Homeowners will adopt Testo measuring instruments if they perceive the devices as a status symbol or premium lifestyle product, because they associate the brand with professional quality and modern home ownership. Who benefits: Affluent homeowners and early adopters who value brand prestige and design.. Why behaviour changes: They will purchase Testo instruments as a statement of quality and as a way to differentiate their home, even if the primary need is not professional measurement.. How value is captured: Testo can capture value through premium pricing, limited-edition designs, and direct-to-consumer branding that emphasizes professional heritage and modern aesthetics.. Assumptions: Affluent homeowners are willing to pay a premium for brand prestige.; Testo can differentiate its consumer offerings with design and branding.; The target segment is reachable through premium retail channels.. Predictions: In a test offering a premium, design-focused version, purchase intent will be higher than for a standard B2B version.; Surveyed homeowners will cite brand prestige and design as the primary reason for choosing the product..

Test "Consumer Proposition Test: Reliability vs. Status Messaging" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated purchase offer and choice-based conjoint.. Sample: 500 homeowners (200 per arm) recruited via a panel to match demographic distribution of target segments (DIY vs. premium).. Measure: Purchase intent (binary: would buy) and stated primary reason (open-ended).. Predictions: T1: In the reliability arm, purchase intent will be higher than in the status arm, and ease of use will be cited as the primary reason.; T2: In the status arm, purchase intent will be higher than in the reliability arm, and brand prestige will be cited as the primary reason.. Decision rule: If the difference in purchase intent between the reliability arm and the status arm is >=15 percentage points, proceed with the differentiated proposition aligned with the higher intent arm. If the difference is <15 points, do not invest in a differentiated proposition and focus on existing B2B market.. Cost: 18000 euros, 8 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition targeting homeowners conducting DIY energy efficiency tasks, emphasizing reliability, ease of use, and professional-grade performance. Begin with a limited online pilot to test purchase intent and primary motivation before scaling. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

T1 kept: The simulated result concerns a label printer and packing errors, which does not address consumer demand for reliability or ease of use in Testo instruments. Therefore it does not affect T1. New claim: none. Evidence: SYN-D.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition targeting homeowners conducting DIY energy efficiency tasks, emphasizing reliability, ease of use, and professional-grade performance. Begin with a limited online pilot to test purchase intent and primary motivation before scaling. Target customer: Homeowners and small business owners performing DIY energy audits, retrofits, and home inspections.. Value proposition: A simplified, reliable Testo instrument designed for DIY energy efficiency tasks, offering professional-grade accuracy and ease of use, sold through online channels with optional data analysis services.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Consumer Proposition Test (Reliability vs. Status Messaging) to measure purchase intent and primary motivation. Use the decision rule to decide whether to proceed with a differentiated proposition.. Uncertainty: The size of the consumer market and the willingness to pay a premium for reliability are uncertain. The status-driven segment may also show demand, but evidence is limited.. Would change if: If the test shows purchase intent below 15% for the reliability arm, indicating low consumer demand, the investment would be reconsidered in favor of focusing on the existing B2B market.; If new evidence shows strong consumer demand for status or premium lifestyle positioning, the recommendation would shift toward a status-driven proposition.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

T1: Consumers will adopt a differentiated home ice machine if it is marketed as a premium convenience product that delivers high-quality, chewable ice directly to their homes, and they are willing to pay a premium for convenience and taste. Who benefits: Home consumers seeking convenient, high-quality ice for beverages and food preparation.. Why behaviour changes: Consumers currently obtain ice from grocery stores or convenience shops, which they perceive as less convenient and less fresh. A premium home ice machine would shift their purchase behavior from store-bought ice to a home solution, driven. How value is captured: Hoshizaki would capture value through premium pricing, direct-to-consumer or retail sales, and brand positioning as a premium convenience brand.. Assumptions: Consumers value convenience and taste in ice.; A premium price is acceptable for a differentiated home ice machine.; Hoshizaki can effectively market and distribute a differentiated consumer product.. Predictions: Surveyed consumers will indicate willingness to pay at least 20% more for a home ice machine compared to store-bought ice.; Purchase intent will be higher for a premium-priced home ice machine than for a standard commercial ice machine.; Sales in a pilot retail or direct-to-consumer channel will exceed a threshold of 100 units per month..

T2: Consumers will adopt a differentiated home ice machine if it is marketed as a sustainable, eco-friendly product that reduces waste and energy consumption, and they are willing to pay a premium for environmental benefits. Who benefits: Environmentally conscious consumers who seek sustainable home appliances.. Why behaviour changes: Growing consumer awareness of environmental impact drives demand for products that reduce waste and energy use. A sustainable home ice machine would align with these values, prompting purchase despite higher cost.. How value is captured: Hoshizaki would capture value through premium pricing, eco-branding, and potential partnerships with sustainability-focused retailers or organizations.. Assumptions: Consumers associate sustainability with product quality and value.; A premium price is acceptable for a sustainable home ice machine.; Hoshizaki can effectively communicate environmental benefits to consumers.. Predictions: Surveyed consumers will indicate willingness to pay at least 15% more for a sustainable home ice machine compared to a standard commercial ice machine.; Purchase intent will be higher for a sustainable-priced home ice machine than for a standard-priced home ice machine.; Sales in a pilot eco-focused retail channel will exceed a threshold of 50 units per month..

Test "Premium vs. Sustainable Home Ice Machine Purchase Intent Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging and willingness-to-pay (WTP) questions.. Sample: 500 U.S. households (200 per arm) recruited via an online panel to match demographic distribution.. Measure: 1) Purchase intent: "Would you buy a home ice machine at a premium price (20% above standard) for convenience and taste?" (binary: Yes/No). 2) WTP: "How much more would you pay for a premium-priced home ice machine compared to a standard-priced home ice machine?" (WTP in euros). 3) Environmental preference: "Which feature matters more: convenience/taste (premium) or sustainability (eco-friendly) when choosing a home ice machine?" (binary: Convenience/Taste vs. Sustainability).. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and WTP for the premium-priced home ice machine (Convenience/Taste) compared to the standard-priced home ice machine.; T2: Higher purchase intent and WTP for the sustainable-priced home ice machine (Sustainability) compared to the premium-priced home ice machine.. Decision rule: If the premium-priced home ice machine meets or exceeds the threshold of 15% higher purchase intent and WTP than the standard-priced home ice machine, proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition focused on premium convenience. If the sustainable-priced home ice machine meets or exceeds the threshold, develop a differentiated proposition focused on sustainability. If neither arm meets its threshold, do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition and maintain current commercial focus.. Cost: 18000 euros, 8 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that positions a premium home ice machine as a convenience product offering high-quality, chewable ice directly to consumers. Begin with a limited pilot in select retail or direct-to-consumer channels to test demand and willingness to pay before scaling. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that positions a premium home ice machine as a convenience product offering high-quality, chewable ice directly to consumers. Begin with a limited pilot in select retail or direct-to-consumer channels to test demand and willingness to pay before scaling. Target customer: Home consumers who value convenience, taste, and are willing to pay a premium for a direct-to-home ice solution.. Value proposition: A premium-priced home ice machine that delivers fresh, chewable ice directly to consumers, offering convenience and superior taste compared to store-bought ice.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Premium vs. Sustainable Purchase Intent Test (500 U.S. households, 8 weeks, €18,000) to measure willingness to pay and purchase intent for a premium-priced home ice machine versus a standard-priced home ice machine.. Uncertainty: The actual willingness to pay for a premium home ice machine and the size of the consumer market remain uncertain. Evidence of strong demand and price elasticity is needed before committing resources.. Would change if: If the test shows purchase intent for the premium-priced home ice machine is below 15% of respondents, indicating low demand for a premium convenience product.; If new evidence shows that environmental sustainability is the primary driver of consumer choice, shifting the recommendation toward a sustainable home ice machine.; If a competitor launches a successful premium home ice machine, indicating strong consumer demand for a differentiated product.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Who benefits: Homeowners and renters who need reliable safety monitoring for CO, alcohol, or other hazards.. Why behaviour changes: They perceive Dräger as a trusted medical/safety brand and are willing to pay a premium for a product that has been used by police and professionals.. How value is captured: Dräger can sell differentiated consumer products at higher margins through its existing retail channels (e.g., online, hardware stores) and capture repeat purchases.. Assumptions: Consumers are aware of Dräger’s professional use.; The brand perception translates into purchase intent.; Retail distribution exists for consumer safety products.. Predictions: A survey of homeowners will show higher purchase intent for Dräger’s consumer devices compared to generic alternatives.; Sales of Dräger’s consumer devices will be concentrated in regions where the brand is already known (e.g., Germany, Austria)..

T2: Consumers will adopt Dräger’s safety technology for home use because regulatory requirements (e.g., CO alarms, breathalyzers) make compliance mandatory, and Dräger’s devices meet or exceed those standards. Who benefits: Homeowners and renters who must purchase safety devices to comply with local regulations.. Why behaviour changes: They purchase devices to avoid fines, insurance penalties, or legal consequences, rather than out of personal safety concern.. How value is captured: Dräger can sell compliant devices through retail channels and capture volume sales, leveraging its existing regulatory certification to differentiate in a crowded market.. Assumptions: Regulatory requirements for safety devices exist in target markets.; Dräger’s devices meet or exceed those requirements.; Consumers are aware of and motivated by compliance requirements.. Predictions: In regions with strict CO alarm regulations, Dräger’s consumer devices will show higher purchase rates than generic alternatives.; Sales will be concentrated in areas where compliance is mandatory (e.g., Washington State, Germany)..

Test "Consumer Messaging Test for Home Safety Devices" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Participants are recruited from German and Austrian households. Half see a product description emphasizing Dräger’s professional reputation and police-grade technology (message A). The other half see the same description but framed as a compliance requirement for CO alarms (message B). Both groups are shown a price point of €334.44 for a personal breathalyzer. The test measures purchase intent (binary: "Would you buy this device?") and stated willingness to pay (WTP).. Sample: 400 participants (200 per condition) recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and region (Germany and Austria).. Measure: Purchase intent rate (percentage of participants indicating "Would you buy this device?" is yes) and average WTP (EUR).. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and WTP for message A (professional reputation) than for message B (compliance).; T2: Higher purchase intent and WTP for message B (compliance) than for message A.. Decision rule: If purchase intent for message A is at least 10 percentage points higher than for message B, proceed to develop a consumer proposition emphasizing professional reputation. If purchase intent for message B is at least 10 percentage points higher than for message A, proceed to develop a compliance-focused consumer proposition. If the difference is less than 10 points, no expansion is recommended.. Cost: 18000 euros, 8 weeks.
