Test "DIY vs Grant Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two conditions: Condition A sees a "DIY" yet professional-grade messaging (e.g., "Professional-grade insulation for homeowners, installed by experts, with a simple DIY guide"). Condition B sees a "Grant‑eligible" messaging (e.g., "Insulation upgrade funded by SEAI grant, save up to €2,000"). Both conditions include a product description, price, and a "Buy Now" button. The decision rule is: if the condition with the higher click‑through rate wins by at least 10 percentage points, that theory is supported. If the difference is ≤ 5 points, the test is inconclusive and a larger experiment is recommended.. Sample: 500 homeowners recruited via an online panel, balanced across the two conditions (250 per condition). Recruitment targets homeowners who have completed a home energy audit or are interested in retrofits.. Measure: Click‑through rate on the "Buy Now" button for each condition.. Predictions: T1: Condition A will have a higher click‑through rate than Condition B by at least 10 percentage points.; T2: Condition B will have a higher click‑through rate than Condition A by at least 10 percentage points.. Decision rule: If Condition A’s click‑through rate exceeds Condition B’s by ≥ 10 percentage points, T1 is supported. If Condition B’s click‑through rate exceeds Condition A’s by ≥ 10 percentage points, T2 is supported. If the difference is ≤ 5 points, the test is inconclusive and a larger experiment is recommended.. Cost: 8000 euros, 4 weeks.

Test "Premium vs Eco‑Certified Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants view a product description of a Franke coffee machine (identical spec‑s) and are asked to indicate purchase intent on a 7‑point scale (1‑not interested to 7‑very interested). The description is presented with one of two messaging frames: (A) premium‑focused (highlighting professional quality, convenience, and modern design) or (B) eco‑focused (highlighting water‑saving, carbon‑neutral, and sustainable materials). Randomly assigned to either frame.. Sample: 300 adult consumers in Germany and Switzerland, recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and income. Stratify by home‑coffee‑machine purchase frequency (annual) to capture both occasional and frequent buyers.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑to 7) for each messaging condition.. Predictions: T1: Premium frame will yield a higher average purchase intent score than eco frame.; T2: Eco frame will yield a higher average purchase intent score than premium frame.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent score for the premium frame is at least 1.5 points higher than the eco frame, proceed to develop a premium‑focused consumer proposition. If the difference is less than 1.5 points, do not invest in a differentiated proposition and continue focusing on professional machines.. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

sources.excerpt: In 2010, bystanders administered CPR in 61 percent of public cases and 28.3 percent of in-home cases. In 2014, the rate of bystander CPR rose to 70.6 percent of public cases and 41.3 percent of in-home cases.

Laerdal Medical is a global leader in healthcare education and resuscitation training, using advanced technology and data-driven insights to improve survival rates and enhance the quality of care. We empower our heroes and lifesavers – healthcare professionals – to help them save more lives.

CPR Anytime is a flexible program that allows you to learn CPR at your own pace, in the comfort and privacy of your home. The kits can also facilitate large CPR training programs in school, workplace, or community settings. The kit is portable, making it easy to share with family members or close friends – resulting in more people trained.

At a time marked by geopolitical instability, war in Europe, and growing demands for national preparedness, Laerdal is strengthening its focus on competence, learning, and collaboration in emergency medical services, both civilian and military.

LEBANON – The intensive care nursery (ICN) at Children’s Hospital at Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center (CHaD), New Hampshire’s only children’s hospital, recently received a donation of 500 Infant CPR Anytime kits from the American Heart Association (AHA), funded by the Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield Foundation. The kits contain tools to help new parents learn the lifesaving skills of infant CPR and infant choking relief in as little as 20 minutes and are being distributed to families being discharged from the ICN.

T1: Homeowners will adopt Dräger’s consumer personal safety devices because they trust the brand’s medical and safety reputation, and will pay a premium for proven reliability. Who benefits: Homeowners seeking reliable home safety solutions and Dräger, which can command higher prices due to its established credibility.. Why behaviour changes: If homeowners perceive Dräger as a trusted medical/safety brand, they are more likely to purchase a device they believe will protect them or their families, rather than a cheaper, unbranded alternative.. How value is captured: Dräger can capture value by selling premium-priced devices under its own brand, leveraging its existing safety division to reach consumers directly or through retail partners.. Assumptions: Homeowners are aware of Dräger’s medical/safety reputation.; Consumers are willing to pay a premium for a brand they trust.; Dräger can reach consumers through existing channels (e.g., online, retail) without major re‑structuring.. Predictions: In a test offering a Dräger consumer device at a premium price, purchase intent among homeowners will be higher than for a comparable unbranded device.; Surveyed homeowners will cite trust in Dräger’s medical/safety reputation as a primary reason for choosing the device..

T2: Homeowners will adopt Dräger’s consumer devices because regulatory requirements (e.g., CO alarms, breathalyzers) make compliance mandatory, and they purchase devices that meet these standards rather than for personal preference. Who benefits: Homeowners who must comply with local safety regulations and Dräger, which can capture value by selling compliant devices through existing channels.. Why behaviour changes: If a device is required by law, homeowners will purchase it to avoid fines or penalties, regardless of brand trust or personal preference.. How value is captured: Dräger can capture value by selling compliant devices at scale, leveraging its existing safety division to meet regulatory demands and potentially expand into new markets.. Assumptions: Local regulations require specific safety devices for homes.; Homeowners are aware of and must comply with these regulations.; Dräger can obtain certification or compliance for its devices.. Predictions: In a test offering a required‑compliant device, purchase intent among homeowners will be higher than for a comparable non‑required device.; Surveyed homeowners will cite regulatory compliance as the primary reason for choosing the device..

Test "Brand Trust vs Regulatory Compliance Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with a simulated purchase scenario. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two conditions: Brand Trust Condition (showing Dräger’s medical/safety reputation and premium pricing) or Regulatory Compliance Condition (highlighting required CO alarms and breathalyzer laws). Both conditions present a Dräger consumer device (e.g., CO detector or breathalyzer) at a fixed price point. Participants indicate purchase intent (1‑ 7 scale) and the primary reason for choosing the device.. Sample: 300 homeowners recruited via an online panel, balanced across Brand Trust and Regulatory Compliance conditions.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑ 7 scale) and the primary reason stated (brand trust vs regulatory compliance).. Predictions: T1: Higher purchase intent and stated brand trust in the Brand Trust Condition than in the Regulatory Compliance Condition.; T2: Higher purchase intent and stated regulatory compliance in the Regulatory Compliance Condition than in the Brand Trust Condition.. Decision rule: If Brand Trust Condition purchase intent ≥ 5 points higher than Regulatory Compliance Condition purchase intent (i.e., Brand Trust ≥ Regulatory Compliance + 5 points), recommend developing a differentiated consumer proposition based on brand trust. If Regulatory Compliance Condition purchase intent ≥ 5 points higher than Brand Trust Condition purchase intent (i.e., Regulatory Compliance ≥ Brand Trust + 5 points), recommend a compliance‑focused consumer proposition. If neither condition meets the 5‑point threshold, recommend no expansion into a consumer proposition at this time.. Cost: 18000 euros, 8 weeks.

Favours T1: Do not yet commit to a consumer proposition. Public evidence shows Dräger’s devices are available and popular (e.g., CO detector sales, breathalyzer listing), but it does not demonstrate that homeowners trust the brand or are willing to pay a premium. A small-scale test (Brand Trust vs Regulatory Compliance) is needed to measure purchase intent differences before any investment. Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Do not yet commit to a consumer proposition. Target customer: Homeowners seeking reliable home safety solutions, particularly those who are aware of and must comply with local safety regulations (e.g., CO alarms, breathalyzers).. Value proposition: A differentiated consumer proposition that leverages Dräger’s established medical and safety reputation to offer premium‑priced, compliant devices, whether sold under Dräger’s own brand or through existing channels.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Brand Trust vs Regulatory Compliance Test (300 homeowners, 8 weeks, €18,000) to determine whether purchase intent differences justify further investment.. Test "Consumer Preference Test: Space vs Sustainability Messaging" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging condition. Participants are recruited from homeowners with limited kitchen space (≤15 sq ft). They view a product description of a Winterhalter undercounter dishwasher, then choose between two messaging conditions: (A) space-saving undercounter unit with multi-functional use; (B) sustainable eco-friendly product with lower carbon footprint. They also indicate willingness to pay (WTP) and purchase intent on a 7-point scale.. Sample: 300 homeowners (150 per condition) recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, gender, and kitchen size.. Measure: Primary outcome: purchase intent (percentage choosing the respective condition). Secondary outcomes: average WTP (EUR) and self-reported importance of space savings vs sustainability.. Predictions: T1: Condition A will generate higher purchase intent than Condition B because space savings and multi-functional use are the primary purchase drivers.; T2: Condition B will generate higher purchase intent than Condition A because sustainability is the primary purchase driver.. Decision rule: If purchase intent for Condition A exceeds Condition B by ≥10 percentage points, conclude T1 is supported. If purchase intent for Condition B exceeds Condition A by ≥10 percentage points, conclude T2 is supported. If the difference is <5 percentage points, both theories remain plausible and further testing is needed.. Cost: 2000 euros, 4 weeks.

DANBURY, Conn. — Belimo Americas, a manufacturer of damper actuators and control valves for commercial HVAC, announced the availability of products for residential applications with select actuators, round damper assemblies, and pressure bypass damper controls.

Total revenue for 2025 is expected to be USD 33.3 million dollar with 7% growth in the Business segment and 21% growth in the Pro segment, while Consumer revenues decreased 20% following the strategic decision to prioritize margin improvement.

Gross profit grew year-on-year in the Business and Pro segments, while gross profit in the Consumer segment was impacted negatively by a weakening US consumer sentiment, US tariffs and costs related to promotions and campaigns with key retail partners.

Belimo is a global market leader in the development, production, and sales of field devices for the energy-efficient control of heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems. The focus of its core business is on damper actuators, control valves, sensors and meters.

With an emphasis on product quality, durability with minimal maintenance, and highly innovative, technically advanced solutions, the Company has become a preferred choice in high-performance applications in large commercial buildings such as data centers, hospitals, schools and universities, offices, governmental buildings, infrastructure and industrial sites.

Belimo collaborates closely with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) of HVAC systems and system integrators who incorporate Belimo products into large-scale HVAC projects. It provides them with extensive technical support, including planning, customization, calibration, and troubleshooting – and conducts training for HVAC professionals to optimize installation effectiveness.
The company’s first product launch of 2020 offers HVAC contractors reliable, high-quality solutions with precise performance and offers the value-conscious homeowner a wider range of options.
In addition to our growing portfolio of DIY solutions sold through top retail and e-commerce channels, the majority of our technologies are installed by professionals.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether there is sufficient public evidence to justify Belimo Holding AG investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current HVAC actuators, valves, and sensors, sold to commercial building manufacturers and through controls contractors and system integrators.. Constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Evidence must demonstrate consumer demand, willingness to pay, or a viable route to market for a differentiated consumer proposition.; Any recommendation must consider Belimo’s existing B2B business model and current reach to individual buyers.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., residential home automation, DIY HVAC control, or a new consumer segment).; 2) Expand the existing B2B product portfolio with new features or packaging without targeting consumers directly.; 3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on commercial building manufacturers and system integrators.; 4) Change the route to market (e.g., direct-to-consumer e‑commerce, partnerships with home‑im improvement retailers, or a subscription model for home control services).; 5) Target a different customer group within the commercial segment (e.g., small‑to‑medium office buildings, residential building owners, or energy‑efficient retrofits)..

Sample: 500 U.S. homeowners (aged 25-55) recruited via an online panel, balanced for income and region.. Measure: Purchase intent (binary: would buy) and maximum willingness-to-pay (WTP) for each product variant.. Predictions: T1: Homeowners exposed to energy-saving metrics will show higher purchase intent and WTP than those exposed to brand reputation metrics.; T2: Homeowners exposed to brand reputation metrics will show higher purchase intent and WTP than those exposed to energy-saving metrics.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent for the energy-saving variant exceeds the brand-reputation variant by at least 10 percentage points, conclude T1 is more supported. If the brand-reputation variant exceeds the energy-saving variant by at least 10 percentage points, conclude T2 is more supported. If the difference is below 10 percentage points, the test is inconclusive and further data is needed.. Cost: 15000 euros, 6 weeks.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether there is sufficient public evidence to justify Kingspan Group plc investing in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its current B2B insulation and building envelope products.. Constraints: Limited to public sources; no internal company data available.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeframe for any proposed experiment.; Need to identify existing consumer reach (e.g., direct‑to‑consumer sales, retail partnerships) and demand for a differentiated product.; Evidence must demonstrate consumer willingness to purchase, current market size, and potential value capture for Kingspan.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting a specific use case (e.g., homeowner DIY insulation, small‑scale building retrofits).; 2) Expand the existing B2B insulation and building envelope products into new professional segments (e.g., larger construction firms, public‑building contractors).; 3) No expansion: continue focusing exclusively on the current B2B market without introducing a consumer proposition.; 4) Partner with existing consumer brands or retailers to bring Kingspan products to individual buyers (e.g., retail distribution of insulation panels).; 5) License the insulation technology to consumer‑focused manufacturers rather than selling under the Kingspan brand..

T1: Homeowners will adopt Kingspan insulation products if they perceive them as a reliable, energy‑efficient upgrade, and will purchase directly through a consumer‑focused channel. Who benefits: Kingspan gains higher margins and direct revenue from individual buyers, while homeowners gain improved home comfort and reduced energy bills.. Why behaviour changes: Growing awareness of energy efficiency and government incentives (e.g., SEAI grants) make insulation a financially attractive DIY project.. How value is captured: Kingspan can sell through its own website or a dedicated consumer hub at premium prices, capturing value through direct sales rather than relying on distributors.. Assumptions: Homeowners are willing to purchase insulation products online and follow DIY installation guides.; Kingspan can deliver trust through product quality and support.; Energy‑efficiency incentives remain active in target markets.. Predictions: A survey of homeowners in target markets will show >50% indicating intent to purchase insulation for energy savings.; Online sales conversions (e.g., orders placed) will be higher than B2B order volumes.; Return rates for DIY kits will be lower than for professional‑delivered products..

T2: Homeowners will adopt Kingspan insulation if they receive professional installation through a trusted partner, because they trust experts to ensure proper installation and compliance with building codes. Who benefits: Kingspan gains higher margin professional sales and repeat business, while homeowners gain guaranteed quality and safety.. Why behaviour changes: DIY installation carries risks of improper insulation, leading homeowners to prefer professional installation for peace of mind.. How value is captured: Kingspan can charge premium prices for professional kits and offer maintenance or upgrade services, capturing value through bundled services.. Assumptions: Professional installation is a perceived risk for DIY homeowners.; Kingspan has a network of certified installers or can partner with contractors.; Regulatory compliance is a key purchase driver.. Predictions: Homeowners will show higher purchase intent when presented with professional installation options compared to DIY kits.; Professional kits will have lower return rates than DIY kits.; Sales will be concentrated in regions where professional building services are already established..

Test "Consumer Proposition Test: DIY vs Professional Installation" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated purchase and installation choice. Participants are recruited from UK homeowners who have completed a home energy audit. They view a product description of Kingspan Kooltherm insulation and are presented with two options: (1) purchase a DIY kit with installation instructions and delivery, or (2) book a professional installation through a partner. They are asked to indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and whether they would choose professional installation (yes/no).. Sample: 400 UK homeowners who have completed a home energy audit, recruited via an online panel. Stratified by region and income to reflect diverse market segments.. Measure: Primary measure: purchase intent score (1‑10) for each option. Secondary measure: binary choice of whether they would choose professional installation versus DIY.. Predictions: T1: DIY purchase intent will be higher than professional installation intent, and the difference will be statistically significant (p<0.05).; T2: Professional installation intent will be higher than DIY purchase intent, and the difference will be statistically significant (p<0.05).. Decision rule: If DIY purchase intent ≥ 55 and professional installation intent ≤ 45, proceed with a differentiated consumer proposition targeting DIY homeowners. If professional installation intent ≥ 55 and DIY purchase intent ≤ 45, pursue professional installation as the primary consumer proposition. If neither threshold is met, do not expand into consumer sales.. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition targeting DIY homeowners, leveraging Kingspan’s existing direct‑to‑consumer sales channel and energy‑efficiency messaging. Begin with a limited pilot of a consumer‑focused hub offering DIY kits and installation guides, using the proposed test to validate purchase intent and professional‑installation preference before scaling. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition targeting DIY homeowners, leveraging Kingspan’s existing direct‑to‑consumer sales channel and energy‑efficiency messaging. Begin with a limited pilot of a consumer‑focused hub offering DIY kits and installation guides, using the proposed test to validate purchase intent and professional‑installation preference before scaling. Target customer: UK homeowners who have completed a home energy audit and are looking to upgrade their home’s insulation efficiency.. Value proposition: Kingspan’s trusted insulation products delivered directly to consumers through a consumer‑focused hub, offering clear DIY installation guidance and energy‑saving benefits, at premium prices that reflect quality and convenience.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Consumer Proposition Test (DIY vs Professional Installation) to measure purchase intent and professional‑installation preference. Use the decision rule to decide whether to proceed with a consumer proposition or focus on B2. Uncertainty: The size of the consumer market and actual purchase intent are uncertain. Evidence shows homeowners are aware of insulation options but have low intent to act (6.3% plan to install in 12 months). The test will clarify whether DIY demand is. Would change if: If the test shows DIY purchase intent ≥ 55 and professional installation intent ≤ 45, we would proceed with a consumer proposition targeting DIY homeowners.; If the test shows professional installation intent ≥ 55 and DIY purchase intent ≤ 45, we would pursue professional installation as the primary consumer proposition.; If neither threshold is met, we would not expand into consumer sales.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.
